original_2: Drinking coffee improves memory. So far this has only been tested in university students. It only showed up after a night without sleep. The improvement was 2 percent on a single word-list test.

retelling: Three startup software teams said remote work boosted productivity, but the gain faded after six months.
original_1: Working from home raises productivity. The evidence comes from one call-centre company in China. Only staff who volunteered to work from home were included. The gain was 13 percent and came mostly from taking fewer breaks.
original_2: The evidence comes from software teams at three start-ups. Productivity was measured by asking people to rate themselves. The gain had disappeared after six months. Working from home raises productivity.

retelling: Coffee seemed to give sleep-deprived students a small memory lift on one word test.
original_1: So far this has only been tested in mice. The dose was the equivalent of eight cups a day. The effect wore off after about two hours. Drinking coffee improves memory.
original_2: Drinking coffee improves memory. So far this has only been tested in university students. It only showed up after a night without sleep. The improvement was 2 percent on a single word-list test.

retelling: A reading app helped English-learning children read, compared with no teaching, but the gains faded by next school year.
original_1: The children in the study already had a private tutor. The app was tested for four weeks. It improved letter recognition but not understanding of stories. The reading app helps children learn to read.
original_2: The reading app helps children learn to read. The children in the study were learning English as a second language. The app was compared with no teaching at all. The gains had faded by the next school year.

retelling: A four-day week in Icelandic public offices reduced burnout, with pay unchanged and no change in sick days.
original_1: A four-day week reduces burnout. The trial was run in public-sector offices in Iceland. Pay was kept the same throughout. The number of sick days did not change.
original_2: The firms in the trial had all volunteered for it. There was no comparison group. Weekly hours only fell from 38 to 34. A four-day week reduces burnout.

retelling: Pesticides harmed bumblebees: one season in two English counties left colonies with a quarter fewer queens.
original_1: This was observed in bumblebees, not honeybees. The study covered one season in two English counties. Colonies produced a quarter fewer queens. The pesticide harms bees.
original_2: The pesticide harms bees. This was observed in laboratory colonies. The doses were ten times what bees meet in fields. It shortened foraging trips but did not kill colonies.

retelling: A small six-week trial of over-65s found daily walks lowered blood pressure, only in non-medicated people.
original_1: A daily twenty-minute walk lowers blood pressure. The study only included adults over 65. It was a small trial of 48 people that ran for six weeks. The drop was about 3 points, and only in people not taking medication.
original_2: The study only included office workers under 40. It was a survey of 12,000 people, so it cannot show cause. The drop was about 11 points, and only in people who also cut down on salt. A daily twenty-minute walk lowers blood pressure.

original_2: Working from home raises productivity. The evidence comes from one call-centre company in China. Only staff who volunteered to work from home were included. The gain was 13 percent and came mostly from taking fewer breaks.

retelling: Small, mixed-quality trials suggest vitamin D prevents colds, but only in people who are deficient in it.
original_1: The benefit was found only in children under five. It comes from a single trial paid for by a supplement maker. It was seen only in the winter months. Vitamin D supplements prevent colds.
original_2: Vitamin D supplements prevent colds. The benefit was found only in people who were deficient to begin with. It comes from pooling 25 small trials of mixed quality. It amounts to one fewer cold a year for every 30 people.
